Sourcing

Questions to ask a packaging supplier

Ask for the company profile, relevant documents, sampling scope and a written specification. Confirm which information applies to the exact material and order.

In this guideStart with requirementsCompare the specificationReview a physical samplePrepare the next step

Start with the Product Requirements

Ask for the company profile, relevant documents, sampling scope and a written specification. Confirm which information applies to the exact material and order.

Record the dimensions and weight of each item, the number of pieces in the set and any supporting accessories. Consider the storage, packing and presentation needs together rather than choosing the outside dimensions first.

Compare a Clear Written Specification

A useful comparison includes the box structure, paper or board, printed areas, finishing processes, insert design and packing method. Ask how each choice affects the sample, production plan and final quote.

Use physical material references where possible. Screen colors and photographs are helpful for direction, but they do not replace an approved paper swatch or print proof.

Check the Physical Sample

Place the actual product inside the proposed packaging. Check the internal fit, opening and closing action, arrangement of accessories and the feel of the materials. Record approved changes before production is confirmed.

For paper-led or mixed-material packaging, review the components individually. Verify any material, testing or environmental statements for the exact order before using them in your marketing.

Prepare a Practical Inquiry

Share product measurements, expected quantities, artwork references, preferred finishing, delivery destination and target timing. A packaging project can begin with a clear description even when the artwork is still being developed.
